Localisation#

With a small ensemble, the covariance between a state far from an observation and that observation is mostly sampling noise. Localisation limits an observation to the states it can plausibly inform. pyCATHY has two unrelated mechanisms; choose by the kind of data.

  • Which mechanism for which data

  • Domain localisation

  • Covariance localisation (a matrix)

  • Choosing

Which mechanism for which data#

Data

Domain localisation (localisation=)

Covariance localisation (matrix)

maps of soil moisture, ET, EM (observed on every surface node)

yes: "nodes", "zones", "veg_map"

yes

ERT (apparent resistivity)

no: raises Cannot localise with apparent resistivity data.

yes, the only option

point sensors (tensiometers, a few probes)

no: fails in _DA_analysis

yes (one column per sensor)

Domain localisation#

AnalysisConfig(localisation=...) (or DAConfig) takes one of "nodes", "zones", "veg_map"; a list with more than one entry is an error. The domain is cut into groups of surface nodes, one analysis is run per group, and each analysis uses only the observations of its group.

Mode

Group

Updated in the group

Notes

"nodes"

one surface node

the state of the column below it; all parameters of listUpdateParm (the code logs loc_shortcut)

one analysis per node: expensive. How the parameter results of the many analyses are combined has not been verified

"zones"

one zone of the zone map

the state and the parameter of the zone

zone numbers 1 to K, nodata excluded

"veg_map"

one vegetation class

the state and the parameter of the class (for instance ZROOT0 for class 1)

class numbers 1 to K, nodata excluded

Things to know:

  • A surface observation is extended to every depth of its column: the group of a zone contains all the nodes below the surface nodes of the zone. This is natural for soil moisture maps and wrong for data whose sensitivity changes with depth.

  • A zone or class without any observation is skipped silently; nodes that no group analysed keep their forecast state (a warning is logged).

  • Pairing of parameters. With "zones" or "veg_map" the parameter <name><k> of listUpdateParm belongs to zone or class number k + 1 (ZROOT0 to class 1), whatever its position in the list, and the state entries ("St. var.") are kept for every zone. A zone with no parameter of its own updates the state only. Names without a numeric suffix fall back to the old positional rule (the parameter at position zone + 1, after a leading state entry).

from pyCATHY.DA.cathy_DA import DAConfig, AnalysisConfig

config = DAConfig(analysis=AnalysisConfig(localisation="veg_map"))
simu.run_DA_sequential(
    parallel=True, dict_obs=dict_obs, list_assimilated_obs="all",
    list_parm2update=["St. var.", "ZROOT0", "ZROOT1", "ZROOT2"],
    DA_type="enkf_Evensen2009_Sakov", dict_parm_pert=var_per_dict_stacked,
    config=config,
)

Covariance localisation (a matrix)#

The covariance of each state with each observation is multiplied element by element by a weight in [0, 1] that decreases with their distance. It is available with DA_type="enkf_analysis_localized_with_inflation", and it acts on the states only: the parameters are not localised.

The weight. localisation.gaspari_cohn(r, L) is the compactly supported function of Gaspari and Cohn (1999). It is 1 at r = 0, decreases monotonically, and is exactly zero beyond ``2 L``: L is half the support, not the cut-off radius. L must be positive.

The matrix. localisation.build_localization_matrix(obs_pos, grid_pos, L) returns an array of shape (n_grid, n_obs): loc[i, j] weights state i with observation j. Positions are the rows of obs_pos and grid_pos, in any column order provided both use the same one (grid3d['mesh3d_nodes'] is ordered [y, x, z]). Add the z column to localise in depth.

Giving it to a run. Either one matrix per DA cycle in simu.localisationMatrix (a list indexed by cycle), or AnalysisConfig(localisation_matrix=...) for all cycles.

import numpy as np
from pyCATHY.DA import localisation

nodes = simu.grid3d["mesh3d_nodes"]                 # (n_nodes, 3), [y, x, z]
# one position per observation: for ERT, for instance, the centre of the four electrodes
obs_pos = quadrupole_centres                         # (n_obs, 3) in the same [y, x, z] order
loc = localisation.build_localization_matrix(obs_pos, nodes, L=2.0)   # (n_nodes, n_obs)
simu.localisationMatrix = [loc] * n_cycles

With ERT. The quadrupoles flagged unusable (see mask_bad_ert) are removed from the analysis, and so are their columns of the matrix: give the matrix for all the quadrupoles of the survey and it is cut to the kept ones; a matrix that already has the width of the kept data is used as is; any other width logs a warning and is rejected by the filter. Before this was handled, one excluded quadrupole made the localised filter fail with a shape error.

Choosing#

  • Soil moisture or ET maps, several soil units or vegetation classes with their own parameter: "zones" or "veg_map".

  • Maps with spatially varying parameters and a large ensemble budget: "nodes".

  • ERT, or any data that is not a surface map: a covariance localisation matrix, with z in the positions when the sensitivity depends on depth.

  • Few data and a homogeneous domain: no localisation is needed.
